rationale: Record the staleleader receipt, add the leader-side knowledge it supports and test the last applicability question. Receipt dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea (all four tests passed) reproduced the two earlier witnesses and showed that the node which took over from a follower whose Promise carried the StopSign ended inflated in its own accepted index: accepted 7 over six indices of content, read(5) None and a one-element decided log (event 13), with both other nodes also at accepted 7 and a one-element read (events 12, 14), so the corruption propagates across the authority change. A behavior was added for the candidate leader syncing from a follower, the applicability fact now lists that third producer instance, the interpretation covers all four receipts with their controls, and the last open half of the registered gap is targeted by a successor experiment that enables snapshots through a snapshot-capable entry type.

investigations.discriminator: Whether a snapshot-capable configuration (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) reproduces the same inflation in the two-follower reconnection scenario, as the branch analysis predicts, or takes the snapshot branch and avoids it.

knowledge.statement: The inflated accepted index follows from the resume point being compared against the index the StopSign occupies in the receiving replica's accounting: sync_log computes accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and adds one for a carried StopSign, while the StopSign occupies the index accepted_idx - 1 and the sender attaches it without shifting sync_idx. The condition is therefore sync_idx + suffix.len() >= the StopSign's index, and it does not depend on the snapshot option: the no-snapshot branch passes the caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged (a re-promising follower's accepted index, or a candidate leader's decided index), whereas the snapshot branch passes the compacted index returned by create_diff_snapshot, which is derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign and therefore excludes the StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any LogSync whose stopsign is Some; the snapshot branch is only entered when T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true and the sender's decided index exceeds common_prefix_idx. Observed producer instances: a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() at the same ballot (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63), a follower re-presenting its accepted index when it re-promises in a new term after an ordinary leader change (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), and a candidate leader that syncs from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13). No snapshot-enabled execution has been run; the successor submitted here exercises that option.

knowledge.statement: A candidate leader whose own promise metadata is not the maximum among the promises it collects syncs its own log from the promise metadata of another node: handle_majority_promises passes that promise's LogSync to sync_log together with the maximum decided index, so the candidate's own accepted index is recomputed from that LogSync and can exceed the number of indices it holds when the LogSync's resume point already covers a carried StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Leader candidate in the prepare phase that receives a promise with a higher accepted round; the follower's Promise carries create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx) and its stored StopSign. Observed: after the previously cut-off node took the lead, that leader reported accepted index 7 over six indices of content, read(5) returned None, and its decided-log read from 0 returned one element (receipt dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13; its accepted index was 6 before the stage and the two other nodes were at 7 as well, so the stage cannot separate the leader's own recomputation from the later reported indexes, while the isolated follower cases 11 and 35 do isolate the resume-point effect).

knowledge.assertion: the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index

interpretations.rationale: Four receipts now support one index-space confusion and three of its consequences. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and receives a resume point that covers it ends one index past its content: observed for a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), for a follower that merely re-promised in a new term after an ordinary leader change with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), and now for the leader itself once it takes over from a follower whose Promise carries the StopSign (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13: accepted 7 over six indices, read(5) None, decided-log read one element). In each case the replica's own reconfiguration endpoint flips from true to false and its decided log stops being readable at its real content. (2) When a write quorum of inflated reports reaches a leader, that leader decides the reported index although it holds fewer indices (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24), which then hides the reconfiguration from that leader as well. The newterm stage shows the same progression: the follower that re-promised was inflated (event 11) while the new leader and the cut-off node stayed at 6/6 (events 9, 10), and in the following stage the node that took over was itself inflated (event 13) together with both other nodes at accepted 7 and a one-element decided read (events 12, 14), i.e. the corruption propagates across authority changes. Controls in every run held: the pre-change samples (events 6-8) and the no-reconnect control (events 9-11 of the first receipt) kept accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true and a six-element decided log for every replica. The remaining scope question is the snapshot option, which the submitted successor exercises with an Entry whose Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true, since the source says the same branch is taken whenever the resume point equals the sender's decided index.

e40cd046de9e4f37b5761260b8dc599e-gap-2.explanation: Both halves now have an executed or sourced basis. Leader half: witnessed - after the previously cut-off node took the lead from a follower whose Promise carried the StopSign, that leader reported accepted index 7 while holding six indices of content and its read of index 5 returned None (receipt dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), which matches handle_majority_promises passing the follower's LogSync to sync_log (leader.rs 257-285, follower.rs 13-51). Snapshot half: still unexecuted, but sourced - the snapshot branch of create_log_sync requires the sender's decided index to exceed the resume point, which is equality in the observed configuration, so the no-snapshot branch is taken even when T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true; when the snapshot branch is entered it derives sync_idx from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign, which excludes the StopSign (mod.rs 405-432, internal_storage.rs 385-412, 469-474). The successor submitted with this update exercises the snapshot option directly.

knowledge.assertion: sync_log double-counts the StopSign when the resumed prefix already covers it
a re-synchronized replica's decided log read loses the entries
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log
a candidate leader syncing from a follower is inflated in its own accepted index

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11), and in the newterm case the new leader and the node that received nothing stayed consistent (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 events 9, 10), so the deviation follows a re-synchronization whose resume point covers the StopSign rather than the reconfiguration or the harness.

The leader-side inflation witness is entangled with the propagation stage: when the cut-off node took over, all three nodes ended at accepted 7 with decided 7 and a one-element decided read (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea events 12-14), so that stage shows the leader's own accepted index exceeded its six indices of content but does not by itself separate its recomputation from the followers' later reports; the isolated single-replica cases (event 35 of the second receipt, event 11 of the third) are the clean witnesses of the resume-point effect.

The leader-side phantom decision requires a write quorum of inflated reporters in one term (two of three nodes); a single inflated follower, or one inflated follower plus a node that received nothing, left the leader consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9).

The documented reconfiguration flow (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true), which narrows the window in which a user reads the old instance, but the leader never observes the decision after the corruption and the followers keep reporting it while their decided log silently loses the entries.
limitations: No snapshot-enabled execution had been run when this account was written; the submitted successor runs the same resync scenario with an Entry whose Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true, and the source says that in this scenario the snapshot branch is not entered and that branch would derive sync_idx without the StopSign when it is entered.

Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised: messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and no tick() timers ran, so the observed producers are explicit reconnected() calls and ordinary leader changes with one node cut off.

The consequence is bounded by the sealed configuration: after the StopSign is accepted no further entries can be accepted, so the phantom decided index carries no value and no value can be mis-assigned; the demonstrated effects are the corrupted index accounting, the unreadable or blank decided log and the lost reconfiguration endpoint rather than divergent values.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and other storages' behaviour on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.
Only three-node clusters were exercised; larger clusters and repeated leader changes beyond the one newterm/staleleader sequence were not.
interpretations.joint_history: Four successive invocations of the same harness lineage, read separately and never combined: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 ran experiment 27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-experiment (resync, control), 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 ran 3ed5ddd94bce4e94a2dc5b7bb417c18a-experiment (plus single-follower resync and a read of index 6), 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 ran 3641dc6df2ae4993b82175d7b24cb702-experiment (plus newterm) and dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea ran c29512939dc747b596ef34a0756327aa-experiment (plus the staleleader stage). Same three-node setup and public endpoints; each successor reproduces the earlier witnesses (resync at events 22-24, newterm at event 11) and adds one case.

scope.description: Six cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process: the resync, single, control and newterm cases over the NoSnapshot entry type, plus a snap case over an entry type whose Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true and whose snapshot derives from the entry ids. The snap case repeats the resync scenario (node 3 leads, five entries decided, StopSign decided, then node 1 and node 2 call reconnected(3)) and samples the same public endpoints under the SNAP_* event names.
assumptions: The snap case uses SnapEntry with SnapState implementing Snapshot<SnapEntry>, create/merge over the entry ids, and use_snapshots() returning true; serde derives satisfy the feature-gated Snapshot bounds.
No snapshot or trim call is issued, so the snapshot branch of create_log_sync is only evaluated, not exercised with a non-empty snapshot.
ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } and default ServerConfig (batch_size 1).
Leadership is obtained with try_become_leader() and all SequencePaxos messages are delivered in FIFO order without loss.
excluded: No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: All previously submitted cases are unchanged. The snap case builds three OmniPaxos<SnapEntry, MemoryStorage<SnapEntry>> instances with the same cluster config, makes node 3 leader with try_become_leader(), appends SnapEntry{id: 0..4} and drains the queue, proposes a StopSign with reconfigure() and drains the queue, then has node 1 and node 2 call reconnected(3) and drains again; SNAP_LEADER_ELECTED, SNAP_ENTRIES_DECIDED, SNAP_STOPSIGN_DECIDED and SNAP_AFTER sample get_accepted_idx, get_decided_idx, is_reconfigured, read(5) and read_decided_suffix(0) for all three nodes.
semantic_changes: Adds a snapshot-capable entry type and the snap case; every previously generated case is unchanged.

comparisons.description: Baseline before the reconnection with snapshots enabled: the StopSign is reported at its own index 5.
Baseline before the reconnection with snapshots enabled: the decided log read from index 0 has six elements.
Baseline before the reconnection with snapshots enabled: every replica reports the reconfiguration as decided.
With snapshots enabled, a re-synchronized replica still reports the StopSign at its own index 5.
With snapshots enabled, a re-synchronized replica's decided log read still has six elements.
With snapshots enabled, the leader's decided index stays covered by the entries it holds.
With snapshots enabled, the leader still reports the reconfiguration as decided.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a snapshot-capable Entry (Snapshot::use_snapshots() returns true) and a case that repeats the two-follower reconnection after a decided StopSign, to test whether the snapshot option changes the inflation.
